4. The defendant-opposite parties filed written objection against the aforesaid application under Order 21 rule 32(1) of the Code of Civil Procedure contending inter alia that they have been in continuous possession in the suit property since before and as such there is no question of disobedience of the decree. It was also contended that the plaintiff petitioner has already filed an independent suit for recovery of khas possession in the suit property and as such the decree for permanent injunction has lost all it relevance and it cannot be executed. 

 7. Mr Garib Newaj, the learned Advocate appearing for the petitioner submits that the learned Assistant Judge seriously erred in law in dismissing the petitioner's execution case on the erroneous view that since the plaintiff petitioner has already filed an independent suit for recovery of khas possession in the suit property the question of willful disobedience or violation does not arise and the same has resulted in error in the impugned decision occasioning failure of justice. The learned Advocate further submits that since there is no provision for adducing any evidence in execution proceedings under Order 21 rule 32(1) of the Code of Civil Procedure, the learned Assistant Judge erred in law in rejecting the petitioner's application on the ground that the petitioner did not adduce any evidence in support of his claim of disobedience and the same has occasioned failure of justice. 

 10. In the facts and circumstances of the case and the materials on record, it must be held that the learned Senior Assistant Judge clearly erred in law in dismissing the petitioner's application on the ground that the petitioner has already filed an independent suit for recovery of khas possession in the suit property and as such section under Order 21 rule 32(1) of the Code of Civil Procedure is not available to the petitioner. 

 14. On consideration of the provision under Order 21 rule 32(1) of the Code of Civil Procedure and the decisions cited by the learned Advocate for the petitioner, it is evident that the decree for permanent injunction is executable and consequently the learned Assistant Judge clearly erred in law in dismissing the execution case on the ground that since the decree-holder has already filed an independent suit for recovery of khas possession, no action under Order 21 rule 32(1) of the Code of Civil Procedure is maintainable.
